summary: The q²+1 count is folklore and was already re-derived in reviews/triage-brainstorm-B.md, which also corrects it in characteristic 2. I did the cheap version of the first step: regressing log M_BM(p) (the BM-corrected main term, BM_CORRECTED_COUNT §2) and log(U+1) on (q/p), q < 80, over 1600 primes p ≡ 1 (4) in (100, 30000). M_BM gets the sign right only at q ≤ 7 (q·β = −0.18, −0.10, −0.08, −0.04 against U's −0.37, −0.35, −0.49, −0.09) and misses the q ≡ 2 (3) pattern entirely (q = 11, 17, 23: M_BM +0.03, +0.04, +0.13 against U −0.34, −0.33, −0.18), so the BM main term does not explain the fitted per-prime weights (EVIDENCE).

Bradford–Ionascu Conj. 1.1 (arXiv:1405.4025, read) allows denominators in Q1 ∪ Q3, a cone that contains −ℕ. On the real axis it is therefore trivial (4/(4k+1) = 1/k − 1/(k(4k+1))), contrary to BRAINSTORM/other_rings.md §4, which calls it a 'lottery again'. An exhaustive search (CERTIFIED by the search) found a solution for all 1614 first-quadrant n with N(n) ≤ 2000. The sharper closed-Q1-only cone contains ES exactly as its real slice (PROVED: Im(1/a) ≤ 0 forces real denominators); exhaustive search to N(n) ≤ 4000 finds exactly 12 exceptions, 6 up to n ↦ i·n̄: 2+5i, 3+4i = (2+i)², 4+5i, 5+6i, 10+13i, 2+17i, all of norm ≤ 293 (EVIDENCE of a finite exceptional set). This is a strict strengthening of ES with no new mechanism, so it gives no lever on ES.

Matrix ES for k = 2 is trivially solvable for every n by one identity (PROVED). A = [[2,1],[1,1]] and B = [[1,−1],[−1,2]] are unimodular and positive definite with A + B + I = 4I, so X = nA⁻¹, Y = nB⁻¹, Z = nI are integral positive-definite matrices with X⁻¹ + Y⁻¹ + Z⁻¹ = (4/n)I. Projecting gives numerators ≠ 1 (e.g. 2/n), so nothing transfers to ES.

At every (★) hit p = 4uBC − u − B we have (−uB/p) = −1, so (−uB)^{(p−1)/4} = ±i₀, with i₀ = a/b mod p for p = a² + b² (a odd, b even, both positive). Over 8964 primes p ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 2·10⁵ the split is 48206 / 48199 (+i₀ / −i₀). Every subgroup (p mod 8, p mod 16, (2/p)₄) is within 1.3σ of 1/2, as is a random-A control (13367 / 13492), and the per-prime fraction has mean 0.5003 (EVIDENCE: no quartic bias, consistent with BRAINSTORM/apollonian_reciprocity.md).

Pomerance–Weingartner (arXiv:2511.16817 v2, Table 1, read) sieved 8/n up to 10¹³ (ET's seven congruences, with 4 replaced by m). The only exceptions are n = 1, 2, 3, 11, 17, 131, 241, so the 'extend to 10⁶' step is done in the literature (17 and 241 are the only ones ≡ 1 mod 4). The repo's 8/p data agree (BRAINSTORM/s8_numerator_size_screen.md; data/z52b/raw/m8_pr1e5.txt; BRAINSTORM/y7_mordell_levels.md, whose 8/n covering at level 840 leaves all 6 squares plus 17 other classes uncovered). A covering-family proof of all-even ES is blocked by the square classes, which the M = 8 covering leaves uncovered (y7_mordell_levels: the M = 8 core contains all 6 unit squares), as for m = 4.

The coincidence is explained by a trivial lemma, not a deeper equivalence. An all-even solution forces some denominator ≡ 0 (mod 4) (PROVED: if all v₂ = 1, halving gives 8/p = Σ1/a_i with the a_i odd, and the parity of p(ab+bc+ca) = 8abc is contradictory). So failures of the '4 | some denominator' condition lie inside the 8/p failures, which up to 10¹³ are {17, 241} among p ≡ 1 (4) (Pomerance–Weingartner Table 1); by direct enumeration 17 and 241 have no solution with 4 | a denominator. The two failure sets therefore coincide up to 10¹³, but there is no per-solution bijection: 233 has 15 solutions with 4 | some denominator but only 9 all-even.

The first step (the mod-840 uncovered classes for m = 5 after the small Type I/II identities) is already in BRAINSTORM/y7_mordell_levels.md. That table, PROVED by exhaustive enumeration, leaves 2 unit classes for M = 5 at L = 840, namely n ≡ 1 (mod 420), against Mordell's 6 squares for M = 4. The alternative step (Type I/II at odd squares for m = 5) is in BRAINSTORM/ident_numerators.md §4: odd squares carry Type I/II solutions for m = 5. Pomerance–Weingartner verify m = 5 to 10¹⁸.

I tabulated the largest prime exception P(m) ≤ 10⁵ and the exception counts for m = 5..48 from the existing raw counts (main checkout data/z52b/raw/m*_pr1e5.txt). The table matches PW Table 1 for m ≤ 15 (e.g. 241, 12241, 281, 353, 20521). For m ≥ 24 exceptions reach the top of the range (saturated). On the unsaturated m, log P(m) ≈ m^0.74 and the mean count at p ≈ 7.5·10⁴ scales as m^−1.19 (EVIDENCE, small-m noisy). The literature (PW, m ≤ 30000) already supersedes this, and the table gives no ES-specific lever.
